proposal: The Mandate recommends resetting USAID programming in the Middle East toward private-sector-led development. It would focus development aid on countries such as Morocco and Sudan through joint investment with the UAE and Israel to advance the Abraham Accords, consider cutting aid to states aligned with Iran and limit non-humanitarian aid in Iraq, Lebanon and the Palestinian territories to narrow priorities, reduce mission footprints, and redirect funding from international partners to local entities.
remaining: Accords-linked development assistance or joint investment with the UAE and Israel in countries such as Morocco and Sudan.
A stated policy limiting remaining non-humanitarian aid in Iraq, Lebanon and the Palestinian territories to narrow priorities.
Redirecting Middle East program funding to local entities.
Delivery of the Abraham Accords expansion strategy required by the FY2026 law.

status_summary: In the successor structure the cut-and-shrink elements were carried out through the general 2025 wind-down rather than a Middle East-specific reset: USAID's remaining operations merged into State on 2025-07-01, and the Lead Inspector General reported that the foreign assistance review cancelled 21 USAID programs in Iraq, that five remaining Iraq programs (27 million dollars) moved to State on 2025-07-01 and four of them ended on 2025-12-31, with three embassy assistance specialists coordinating aid. Executive Order 14199 (signed 2025-02-04) barred executive funding of UNRWA, funding for Palestinian Authority security forces was reported halted in February 2025, and the finalized FY2026 State funding package, enacted in Public Law 119-75 on 2026-02-03, was reported to keep the UNRWA ban and require a State strategy within 90 days to expand the Abraham Accords. On the positive agenda, a whistleblower spreadsheet reported in March 2025 listed more than 32 million dollars of Middle East Regional Cooperation grants for Israeli and Arab scientific work as cancelled, which runs against the Accords element, and no Accords-linked development investment in Morocco or Sudan with the UAE and Israel, and no shift of Middle East funds to local entities, was found. Aid to Lebanon continued in other forms: Reuters reported 230 million dollars of security assistance released at the end of September 2025, outside the text's development focus.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14199 (90 FR 9275, published 2025-02-10) provided in Sec. 3(a) that executive departments and agencies shall not use funds for a contribution, grant or other payment to UNRWA, and directed withdrawal of a prior determination under section 7048(c)(1) of division F of P.L. 118-47.

Anadolu, citing officials and a Washington Post report, reported that the US had halted funding for Palestinian Authority security forces as part of the broader foreign aid freeze, with some training programs cancelled.

Cancellations of Middle East foreign assistance grants were documented in a whistleblower spreadsheet shared with the Senate Foreign Relations Committee and released by Punchbowl News, which listed more than 32 million dollars of Middle East Regional Cooperation grants as cancelled and West Bank and Gaza and Lebanon funding as affected, not all confirmed as cancelled (month-only date; as reported by Jewish Insider).

USAID's remaining operations merged into the State Department (as reported by NPR); the Lead Inspector General later reported that five active Iraq programs (27 million dollars) moved to State management that day.

Reuters reported that the administration released 230 million dollars for Lebanon's armed forces (190 million) and Internal Security Forces (40 million) just before the fiscal year ended on 2025-09-30, citing anonymous sources; this is security assistance.
Four of the five legacy USAID Iraq programs ended; the US Embassy in Baghdad had onboarded three assistance specialists, and State had 18 stabilization and 4 humanitarian awards active in Iraq.

Congressional negotiators released the finalized FY2026 State funding package, which keeps the UNRWA funding ban, provides 112.5 million dollars for Lebanon with existing accountability provisions on the Lebanese Armed Forces, keeps existing West Bank and Gaza aid mechanisms and requires a State strategy within 90 days to expand the Abraham Accords (month-only date; as reported by Jewish Insider).
Public Law 119-75 (H.R. 7148, Consolidated Appropriations Act, 2026) was enacted; its Division F is the National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2026.

title: Reset Middle East aid: back the Abraham Accords, cut Iran-aligned aid, shrink footprints
uncertainties: Both Jewish Insider articles carry only month-level dates (from their addresses), and the pages show no day; the first-of-month dates used here are placeholders, not publication dates. The January 2026 article says the finalized package was released on a Sunday and does not report enactment; enactment of Public Law 119-75 on 2026-02-03 and its Division F come from GovInfo. The statutory UNRWA bar and the Abraham Accords strategy requirement are described only through that press report: the GovInfo text of Division F could not be read because the fetched text was cut short, so the section numbers were not confirmed; the executive bar on UNRWA funding rests on Executive Order 14199 (read on the Federal Register). The March 2025 figures come from a whistleblower spreadsheet as reported by Jewish Insider; the article itself distinguishes funding listed as affected (about 1 billion dollars for West Bank and Gaza, about 380 million dollars for Lebanon) from confirmed cancellations, and no primary termination list was read. Terminations came through the global foreign assistance review, not a Middle East reset designed on the text's lines. No Abraham Accords-linked development fund, UAE or Israel co-investment, or Morocco and Sudan assistance announcement was found; the Kazakhstan accession of 2025-11-06 is a diplomatic step, not aid. Local-entity funding for the Middle East was not found. Whether the Abraham Accords strategy required by the FY2026 act was delivered was not checked. Division F of P.L. 119-75 could not be read: the GovInfo HTML of the public law and the enrolled-bill XML of H.R. 7148 both end within Division A, Title VIII, so the UNRWA, Lebanon and Abraham Accords strategy provisions remain sourced to the press report. The Lead Inspector General page and EO 14199 were read directly and match the record.
